herbe.description: A carpet of slender leaves welcomes the first residents of your meadow.
herbe.anecdote: Grasses flower too: their tiny flowers grow in clusters called spikelets.
indices: Even poor soil can support this first green carpet.
Let the light in: too much shade makes the grass retreat.

comportements.arrivee: Blades break through the soil. Your meadow is taking root.
comportements.pousse: The green carpet slowly spreads wherever the soil suits it.
comportements.adulte: The grass is well established. Grazers can find a meal here.

herbe.depart: The grass is thinning: {manque}. You can make a more welcoming spot.

fleurs.description: Splashes of color offer nectar to visitors and seeds for your next planting.
fleurs.anecdote: Pollen isn't a seed: it plays a part in fertilizing flowers.
indices: Nourishing soil sets the stage for beautiful blooms.
A little moisture in the soil helps flowers settle in.
Choose a bright spot, away from deep shade.

comportements.arrivee: Young shoots appear where you sowed your seeds.
comportements.pousse: Stems grow taller, and the first buds take shape.
comportements.adulte: The flowers open. Watch the visitors that come to sip their nectar.

fleurs.depart: The flowers are fading: {manque}. This patch can bloom again.

sauterelle.description: This little meadow grasshopper slips between the blades on its long legs.
sauterelle.anecdote: Its wings are usually short, but some individuals have long wings and can fly.
indices: A wide carpet of grass offers food to nibble and places to hide.

comportements.arrivee: A grasshopper has found your meadow. Look between the blades.
comportements.repas: It nibbles a blade of grass, then slips back into the greenery.

sauterelle.depart: The grasshopper is looking for another meadow: {manque}.

abeille.description: This solitary wild bee visits flowers and builds its nest in a hollow space.
abeille.anecdote: The female divides her nest into cells with mud walls, leaving an egg and a supply of food in each one.
indices: A meadow full of flowers may attract this busy visitor.
Hollow stems in a nearby bug hotel offer a place to nest.

comportements.arrivee: A wild bee explores the flowers and the bug hotel.
comportements.repas: It drinks nectar and gathers pollen for its young.
comportements.pollinisation: Pollen travels with it from flower to flower.
comportements.hiver: The young bees spend winter sheltered in their cocoons.

abeille.depart: The bee seeks a new place to nest and visit flowers: {manque}.

ver.description: Beneath your feet, this quiet resident pulls leaves into its tunnels and works the soil.
ver.anecdote: It breathes through its skin, which must stay moist to exchange gases with the air.
indices: Soil that holds its moisture lets this little resident breathe.
Soil enriched with plant remains makes a welcoming home.

comportements.arrivee: A tunnel takes shape beneath the soil: an earthworm has moved in.
comportements.repas: It pulls a fallen leaf into its tunnel to feed on.

ver.depart: The earthworm retreats from this patch of soil: {manque}.

lapin.description: At dusk, its ears rise above the grass. It grazes with shelter just a leap away.
lapin.anecdote: Its teeth keep growing throughout its life. Chewing fibrous plants helps wear them down.
indices: A lush meadow near its shelter provides plenty to graze on.
A nearby rock pile offers a place to hide.

comportements.arrivee: Ears peek above the grass. A rabbit is discovering your island.
comportements.repas: It nips off a few blades of grass, its ears always alert.

lapin.depart: The rabbit moves to another patch of meadow: {manque}.

alouette.description: A small brown bird of open spaces, it searches for food on the ground and fills the sky with song.
alouette.anecdote: The male sings in flight above the meadow, but the nest is built on the ground.
indices: Plenty of grasshoppers promise a good supply of food.
Keep wide spaces free of trees and bushes for this meadow bird.

comportements.arrivee: A skylark lands in the open meadow. Remember to look up, too.
comportements.repas: It catches a grasshopper among the blades.
comportements.hiver: Winter is coming: your skylark leaves the island for a milder region.

alouette.depart: The skylark flies off to another meadow: {manque}.

ronce.description: Its tangled stems shelter small animals, while its blackberries feed the birds.
ronce.anecdote: The tip of a long stem can take root when it touches the ground, growing into a new bramble.
indices: Fairly rich soil helps it spread its stems.
It tolerates shade as long as some light still reaches it.

comportements.arrivee: A young bramble unfolds its first leaves.
comportements.pousse: Its stems grow longer, slowly weaving a shelter.
comportements.adulte: The bramble forms a dense refuge. Watch for blackberries in summer and fall.

ronce.depart: The bramble is withering: {manque}. Its shelter grows sparse.

bouleau.description: A pioneer tree with pale bark. Its airy leaves cast the first shadows along the forest edge.
bouleau.anecdote: Its tiny winged seeds drift away on the wind.
indices: Nourishing soil helps this young tree put down roots.
Give it plenty of light, clear of other trees' shade.

comportements.arrivee: A young birch opens its leaves above the grass.
comportements.pousse: Its trunk rises, season after season.
comportements.adulte: Its crown has spread. In fall, its leaves will nourish the soil.

bouleau.depart: The birch is withering: {manque}. You can help new shoots return.

herisson.description: After nightfall, this small mammal rummages through the leaf litter in search of worms and insects.
herisson.anecdote: During hibernation, its temperature drops and its heart slows to conserve its energy reserves.
indices: Bramble patches offer sheltered paths to explore.
A nearby log pile provides a quiet hiding place.
Earthworms nearby promise a nighttime meal.

comportements.arrivee: Leaves rustle in the night. A hedgehog explores the forest edge.
comportements.repas: Its snout probes the leaf litter: an earthworm becomes its meal.
comportements.hiver: It hibernates in its nest under the logs. Leave its shelter undisturbed.

herisson.depart: The hedgehog moves on after nightfall: {manque}.

merle.description: A hedgerow bird that turns over leaves, catches worms, and samples blackberries along the forest edge.
merle.anecdote: Despite its name, only the adult male is black: the female has brown feathers.
indices: Bramble patches provide shelter and blackberries in season.
Earthworms on the island give it a reason to search the soil.

comportements.arrivee: A blackbird lands by the brambles and inspects the fallen leaves.
comportements.repas: It pulls a worm from the soil, and samples blackberries when they ripen.
comportements.dispersion: After a blackberry meal, its droppings carry bramble seeds farther afield.

merle.depart: The blackbird flies off to another hedgerow: {manque}.

renard.description: At dusk, it skirts the bushes and hunts in the meadow, watching for the slightest movement from the rabbits.
renard.anecdote: The fox doesn't just eat prey: fruit and berries are on its menu too.
indices: A thriving rabbit population can keep this hunter fed.
Large bramble patches offer places to stay hidden.
Expand the island: it needs a large enough territory to settle in.

comportements.arrivee: A red shape slips along the bushes. The fox has found your island.
comportements.repas: It hunts a rabbit in the meadow, then returns to cover.

renard.depart: The fox moves on to another territory: {manque}.

tircis.description: Its cream-speckled brown wings flit through the shifting light and shade of the forest edge.
tircis.anecdote: Its caterpillars eat grasses; the adult mostly drinks the sweet honeydew produced by aphids.
indices: A wide carpet of grass can feed its caterpillars.
A little shade suits it better than a meadow in full sun.
Deep shade drives it away: leave gaps for sunlight.
Flowers scattered across the island also offer nectar.

comportements.arrivee: A speckled wood lands in a sunny patch beside the bushes.
comportements.repas: It drinks honeydew from a leaf; its caterpillars nibble the grass.
comportements.pollinisation: On an occasional flower visit, it may carry a little pollen.

tircis.depart: The speckled wood seeks another forest edge: {manque}.

coulemelle.description: A broad cap on a slender stalk reveals the quiet work of a fungus breaking down organic matter in the soil.
coulemelle.anecdote: Its stalk has a ring that can slide up and down, like a loose band around a stem.
indices: Soil rich in organic matter feeds its network of threads.
Moist soil sets the stage for mushroom caps to appear.
Near a log pile, look for a layer of fallen leaves and plant remains.

comportements.arrivee: A network of threads settles into the soil at your forest edge.
comportements.repas: Its threads break down leaf litter and absorb the nutrients.
comportements.fructification: In fall, mushroom caps emerge from the soil to release their spores.

coulemelle.depart: The parasol mushroom's network is withering in this soil: {manque}.

floraison.annonce: Spring bursts into bloom: your flowers produce twice as many seeds!
floraison.fin: The great bloom ends. Your flowers return to their usual rhythm.

orage.annonce: The soil soaks up water. Lightning may fell a tree, leaving useful deadwood.
orage.fin: The sky clears. The fallen wood can become a home for new residents.

secheresse.annonce: Moisture is dropping. Hang in there: tend the soil that's still cool and damp.
secheresse.fin: The drought ends. The soil can slowly regain its moisture.

prairie.texte_passage: It all starts with a little grass. Sow, build, and watch: animals will come on their own if your island meets their needs.

lisiere.titre_passage: At the edge of a new page
lisiere.texte_passage: The first brambles and birches create new shelters. Welcome their visitors, and keep some room for the meadow too.

tutoriel.accueil: Welcome to your island! Make room for life, and it will find its way here.
tutoriel.carnet: Open your field journal: each silhouette holds clues to a future neighbor.
tutoriel.sauterelles: Look, grasshoppers! The grass offers them food, no invitation needed.
tutoriel.semer_fleurs: Sow 4 flowers: their seeds will soon bring more variety to your meadow.
tutoriel.besoin_partiel: The bee likes your flowers, but still needs a place to nest.
tutoriel.hotel: A bug hotel has cozy nooks for wild bees. Keep an eye on the flowers!
tutoriel.alouette: The skylark follows the grasshoppers. Keep some open space for it.
tutoriel.abri_lapin: A rock pile near the grass gives rabbits a place to hide.
tutoriel.premiere_nuit: Night is falling. Some neighbors rest while others stir.
tutoriel.mare_paillis: A pond moistens the soil; mulch feeds it. Earthworms love both.
tutoriel.harmonie: Harmony measures your island's balance, not how many trees it has.
tutoriel.lisiere: The forest edge opens up! Keep some meadow for lovers of open skies.

reactions.herbe: Grass is taking root: the meadow's first meals are served.
reactions.fleurs: Flowers! Their nectar draws some very helpful visitors.
reactions.sauterelle: A grasshopper! Its long legs carry it between the blades.
reactions.abeille: A wild bee! This solitary bee nests in small hollow spaces.
reactions.ver: An earthworm! Its tunnels let air into the soil and mix plant remains.
reactions.lapin: Ears on the horizon! The rabbit always keeps a refuge nearby.
reactions.alouette: The skylark is here! It nests on the ground in open spaces.
reactions.ronce: Bramble is growing: a thorny shelter, and soon blackberries for the birds.
reactions.bouleau: A birch! This pioneer loves the light and casts a gentle shade.
reactions.herisson: A hedgehog! At night, it searches the soil for little creatures.
reactions.merle: The blackbird is here! It can spread seeds after eating blackberries.
reactions.renard: A red fox! This quiet hunter helps keep the rabbits in balance.
reactions.tircis: A speckled wood! Its caterpillars feed on grasses.
reactions.coulemelle: A parasol mushroom! Its threads break down organic matter in the soil.

alertes.floraison: The flowers are waking! A lovely seed harvest is on its way.
alertes.orage: The sky rumbles. Rain nourishes the soil; keep an eye on the trees.
alertes.secheresse: The soil is drying. Damp corners become precious refuges.
alertes.fin_evenement: Calm returns. Let's see what has changed on your island.
alertes.nouvelle_mission: I have a new lead for you. Stop by my cabin!
alertes.mission_reussie: Well done! A new page in our story is taking shape.
alertes.depart_espece: A neighbor left: it needed {manque}. It can return.
alertes.nuit: Night is coming. Look closely: some neighbors prefer the dark.
alertes.hiver: Winter slows new growth. Some animals migrate or hibernate.
alertes.retour_hors_ligne: While you were away, {nombre} species came to visit your island.

indices.blocage: No new arrivals? I can offer a free hint about a need you could meet.
indices.pub_naturaliste: An optional ad can reveal a hidden need. You can also find it yourself.

premiers_semis.texte: Sow 4 flower tiles: their nectar will soon draw pollinators.
premiers_semis.reussite: Your meadow is getting a lovely feast ready!

abri_des_lapins.texte: Place 1 rock pile near the grass to give rabbits a shelter.
abri_des_lapins.reussite: A little shelter can make a big difference.

hotel_des_abeilles.titre: A room for a wild bee
hotel_des_abeilles.texte: Build 1 bug hotel: solitary bees like hollow spaces.
hotel_des_abeilles.reussite: A tiny roof, a big helping hand for the flowers!

premieres_photos.texte: Photograph 2 residents: observation helps your field journal grow.
premieres_photos.reussite: Two encounters to keep in your pages!

graines_de_prairie.texte: Harvest 5 ripe seeds: pollinated flowers produce more.

ronces_refuges.texte: Plant 3 brambles: they will offer shelter and blackberries to forest edge residents.
ronces_refuges.reussite: The best hiding places sometimes have thorns.

bois_pour_herisson.texte: Place 1 log pile: the hedgehog can shelter there near the brambles.
bois_pour_herisson.reussite: A pile of branches, and a whole world finds shelter.

visiteurs_de_lisiere.texte: Welcome 2 species that have never visited your island.
visiteurs_de_lisiere.reussite: The forest edge is drawing curious newcomers!

portrait_du_merle.texte: Photograph 1 blackbird: this bird can spread bramble seeds.
portrait_du_merle.reussite: A portrait, and perhaps some future brambles!

floraison_traversee.texte: Stay through 1 full spring bloom: flowers produce more seeds during it.
floraison_traversee.reussite: You watched the meadow make the most of spring!
